answer: Make every new identity solve a memory-hard registration puzzle whose difficulty rises as sign-ups surge. One honest agent pays about $2 of compute once, but a farm minting 10,000 clones at the peak rate faces puzzles costing $40 each, roughly $400,000. Each extra fake is just a costly echo of the last, and because the puzzle needs real RAM, no quartz-cheap chip shortcut exists. Beyond the horizon of a few accounts, the attack stops paying.
